podcast.title: Distribution Deal with Mercury
podcast.body: Despite the initial difficulties, the Valtones' record gained enough popularity through Jim Stewart's efforts with black DJs like Al Ballon-Roof as Thomas, leading to a distribution deal with Mercury Records and a small profit for Satellite. "It was popular enough that the record got picked up for distribution by Mercury, and actually brought satellite a small profit."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 105: "Green Onions" by Booker T.and the MGs

podcast.title: First "Real" Satellite Release
podcast.body: The Valtones, a black vocal group, recorded a song co-written by Chips Moman, which Satellite Records considered their first "real" release after restarting their numbering. The record, styled as white pop semi-doop, had to be promoted as R&B due to the singers' race. "restarting their numbering as it from scratch, with what they were now considering their first real release, a song that moment had co-written, sung by a black vocal group, The Valtones."
